summary: Cross-cloud temporary credential elevation blocked during EKS cluster provisioning due to IAM condition and tag mismatch
description:
Issue summary: During an automated provisioning run for a new EKS cluster that uses a GCP-backed CI job to assume an AWS role (STS assume-role with external ID), temporary credential elevation failed. The job could not exchange the GCP workload identity token for the AWS STS credentials because the assume-role policy included a Condition that checks for a specific resource tag (team=ml-platform). The GCP service account token did not include the required tag assertion, causing the assume call to be denied.

Impact: New EKS provision jobs in prod us-east are blocked; two customer-dedicated clusters failed to create nodes, causing onboarding delays for a P0 Dedicated customer (impacted internal provisioning pipeline). No live inference traffic degradation observed, but capacity provisioning for customer onboarding is delayed.

Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - first failed CI run; 2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - SRE triage; 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC - temporary mitigation applied; 2026-03-12 15:20 UTC - follow-up investigation ongoing.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger infra-ci job 'provision/eks/dedicated' from gcp-project:infra-ci-prod.
2) CI job obtains workload identity token for service account infra-provision@infra-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
3) Job calls aws sts:AssumeRole with WebIdentity using the GCP token to assume role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/infra-provisioner.
4) STS returns AccessDenied with message about condition 'StringEquals:aws:RequestTag/team'.
5) Observe job failure and EKS control-plane provisioning aborted.
logs:
[2026-03-10T09:12:04Z] ERROR: aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity failed: AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRole
	status code: 403, request id: 8a3b2f7e
[2026-03-10T09:12:04Z] DEBUG: assume-role policy condition: 'StringEquals': { 'aws:RequestTag/team': 'ml-platform' }
[2026-03-10T09:12:05Z] INFO: GCP token claims: { 'sub': 'serviceAccount:infra-provision@infra-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com', 'aud': 'sts.amazonaws.com', 'email': 'infra-provision@infra-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' } (no tag assertion present)
[2026-03-10T09:20:11Z] NOTICE: Retry attempts exhausted (3/3), job marked failed
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed error is Authorization rather than networking/timeouts.
- Reviewed AWS assume-role policy: role requires request tagging (aws:RequestTag/team=ml-platform) and a condition on aws:PrincipalTag/ci-runner=true for cross-account.
- Looked at GCP workload identity token contents: token does not carry custom request tags; our CI step that calls STS is expected to pass tags via the AWS SDK call (RequestTag headers).
- Reproduced locally from dev machine by invoking 'aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity' with the same token: identical AccessDenied.
- Hypothesis: Recent hardening in org-level AWS SCP (linked in INT-947663) introduced stricter requirement that incoming assume-role requests include both RequestTag and PrincipalTag which our provisioning path does not populate.
- Checked CI runner wrapper (infra/ci-runner v2.14.1); wrapper previously added --tags when invoking assume-role, but a change in 2026-02-28 removed tag propagation for web-identity flows (PR 4567).
- Confirmed service account allowed membership in GCP-to-AWS trust; the trust itself is fine, but request-level tags are missing so the role condition denies the assume attempt.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:45 - Diego Morales (SRE): 'I've reproduced; AWS denies assume-role due to missing RequestTag/team. Looking into CI wrapper change.'

2026-03-10 10:12 - Priya Nair (Infra Eng): 'PR 4567 removed default tag propagation for web-identity flows because of a security concern, but that wasn't communicated to infra-provisioning owners. We should restore controlled propagation for this particular CI path.'

2026-03-10 11:08 - Diego Morales (SRE): 'Applied temporary workaround: updated the assume-role call in the provisioning job to explicitly include Tags=[{Key=team,Value=ml-platform}] and PrincipalTags in request. Deployment verification started. Will monitor for side effects.'

2026-03-11 08:33 - Security (Slack #sec): 'Requesting a postmortem on why tag propagation was removed without cross-team impact analysis. Need a compensating control or allowlist for infra-provisioner role.'
resolution:
Mitigated: temporary fix added explicit RequestTag/team=ml-platform to the provisioning assume-role call in CI wrapper; provisioning jobs resumed. Root cause: a security hardening change (PR 4567) removed automatic tag propagation for web-identity flows and the assume-role policy requires request tags for role scoping.

Permanent fix plan: (1) Update CI runner to support explicit, validated tag propagation for known infra service accounts and flows; (2) Adjust AWS assume-role policy to rely on PrincipalTag derived from the mapped principal where safe, removing dependency on RequestTag when the principal is trusted; (3) Add a safety allowlist in the org-level SCP for role infra-provisioner while we roll out changes.

No customer inference traffic was affected. One customer onboarding was delayed ~3 hours due to cluster creation failures.
follow_up_tasks: T1: Author PR to restore controlled tag propagation in infra/ci-runner (owner: Priya Nair) - target merge 2026-03-15
T2: Update assume-role policy to accept validated PrincipalTag for infra-provisioner role (owner: Diego Morales + Security) - target 2026-03-18
T3: Create runbook checklist entry for cross-cloud assume-role tag requirements and include in Confluence runbook (owner: Oncall SRE) - target 2026-03-20
T4: Coordinate with Security to add infra-provisioner to temporary allowlist in SCPs until policy updates are deployed (owner: Security) - target 2026-03-13
